newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hopewell says in good financial position.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell says in good financial position.

text.p: Hong Kong-based infrastructure firm Hopewell Holdings Ltd on Friday sought to reject market scepticism about its financial position and its ability to fund its ambitious projects, saying the firm is in a good shape.
"Hopewell has never been in financial difficulty, and is today in very good shape," executive director Robert Niem told a news conference when the firm announced its interim results.

He pointed out Hopewell's financial position had improved after it had repaid debts with cash proceeds of HK$9.74 billion from the sale of its 40.4 perccent stake in Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA) to Southern Co.
The deal, completed in January, reduced its net debt to equity ratio to 34 percent at the end of January from over 90 percent at the end of last June, he noted.
The ratio was 13.6 percent excluding limited recourse debt arranged for its joint venture partners at project level, he said.
Apart from concerns over its gearing, some analysts also have misgivings as to whether the firm is able to fund its projects, particularly its US$3.2 billion mass transit project in Bangkok.
Niem said Hopewell expected no difficulties in securing loans for its projects.
"We've been good in obtaining these project loans from banks," he said. "We work very closely with banks and we have a lot of bankers who support us."
Hopewell is involved in the development and operation of large scale infrastructure, including transport, power generation and property projects, in China and other Asian countries.
Niem did not categorically rule out future fund raising in the equity market such as a rights issue for capital for its projects.
"We are constantly reviewing our fundraising alternatives and options. There are a number of proposals we are considering," he said, declining to be specific.
The firm reported an 89 percent surge in operating profit to HK$769 million for the half-year ended December 31. Its net proift grew 7.7 percent to HK$502 million during the period.

Niem attributed the earnings growth to the opening of new power stations in the Philippines and China, and increased revenue due to increased traffic and tolls from the completed section of the Guangzhou-Shenzhen-Zhuhai Superhighway in southern China.
A growth in contribution from rental properties also helped boost earnings, he added.
After the disposal of its CEPA shares, Hopewell's total net assets rose to HK$27 billion, or HK$6.16 per share.
